title: Roman cult of Saints is analogical, and only loosely called religious or adoration
source_text: II. Cultum eum non contineri sub eodem univoco genere cum eo qui Deo proprius est, sed cum eo solum quandam analogiam habere. Illum tamen posse religiosum dici, non proprie & stricte loquendo, sed latiori & minus propria significatione. Et similiter illi accommodari posse adorationis nomen, licet adoratio saepe ad cultum Deo proprium restringatur.
pass_a_gloss: That cult is not contained under the same univocal genus with the cult proper to God, but has only a certain analogy with it. It can nevertheless be called religious, not speaking properly and strictly, but in a broader and less proper sense. Likewise the name of adoration can be fitted to it, although adoration is often restricted to the cult proper to God.
pass_b_english: Rome does not put Saint-honor in the same univocal class as worship that belongs to God alone.
The link is analogy, not identity of kind.
Religious and adoration may be used of it only in a looser, less proper sense.
In the stricter use, adoration stays reserved for God.

choices.why: Keeps religious and adoration from being claimed as strictly divine names.
rejected: in the proper sense of latria
as a mere metaphor with no cult at all
